blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Despite rapid progress in text-to-motion generation, existing methods are commonly designed for single-shot generation. When users are dissatisfied with specific motion details, they are often forced to regenerate the entire sequence from scratch, which is computationally inefficient and potentially destroys previously established kinematic context. A practical generation system should instead support iterative user feedback and refine only the affected spatio-temporal regions while preserving the remaining motion. Therefore, we introduce a conversational motion generation paradigm that requires the system to coordinate instruction understanding, motion generation, localized editing, and quality assessment. Recent advances in LLM-driven multi-agent systems provide a promising foundation for such role-specialized coordination. To tackle these challenges, a Self-evolving Multi-Agent RefinemenT Framework (SMART) is proposed for conversational motion generation. Within SMART, to preserve semantic consistency, we design a semantic-guided masked motion editing mechanism, which precisely grounds natural language feedback into spatiotemporal motion regions to enable localized refinements without altering unedited regions. To reduce redundant exploration, we propose a memory-based self-evolving strategy that dynamically accumulates motion editing knowledge from interaction history and reuses past successful experience. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMART effectively supports multi-turn conversational motion generation and enables efficient motion refinement.

blocks.en: Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Text-to-Motion (T2M) generation ( Zhu et al. 2023 ; Chen et al. 2024 ; Yu et al. 2024 ) , which aims to synthesize realistic human motions from natural language descriptions, has emerged as a fundamental task with broad applications in gaming, virtual reality, and robotics ( Guo et al. 2025 ; Tashakori et al. 2025 ; Zitkovich et al. 2023 ) .
Despite recent progress, T2M generation remains challenging because it requires both accurate language understanding and faithful translation of textual semantics into temporally coherent motion sequences.
blocks.zh:
文本对动(T2M)生成( Zhu等. 2023; 陈等. ; Yu等. 2024.; 2024.),旨在从自然语言描述中综合出现实人类运动,已经作为一个基本任务出现,在游戏,虚拟现实,机器人方面有着广泛的应用(Guo等2025;Tashakori等2025;Zitkovich等2023.).
尽管最近取得了进展,但T2M生成仍然具有挑战性,因为它既需要准确的语言理解,也需要忠实地将文字语义翻译为时间上一致的运动序列.

blocks.en:
Existing T2M methods have explored diverse generation paradigms.
Autoencoder-based methods ( Zhang et al. 2023b ; Zhong et al. 2023 ; Geng et al. 2024 ) learn compact latent motion representations for synthesis. GAN-based methods ( Ahn et al. 2018 ; Xu et al. 2023 ; Ahuja and Morency 2019 ) improve motion realism through adversarial training. Autoregressive methods ( Jiang et al. 2023 ; Zhang et al. 2023a ; Guo et al. 2022b ) model motions as discrete token sequences. And diffusion-based methods ( Tevet et al. 2022 ; Huang et al. 2024 ; Yang et al. 2023 ) generate motions through iterative denoising.
Recently, driven by rapid advancements in large language models (LLMs) ( Achiam et al. 2023 ; Zhao et al. 2023 ; Li et al. 2025 ) , LLM-based motion generation approaches ( Jiang et al. 2023 ; Wang et al. 2024b ; Wu et al. 2025 ) have made significant strides in generating high-fidelity motions that align with complex textual instructions.

现有的T2M方法已经探索出不同的世代范式.
自动编码法(张等. 2023b; 钟等. 2023; Geng等人,2024)学习紧凑的潜伏运动表达法进行合成. 基于GAN的方法(Ahn等. 2018; 许等. 2023; Ahuja and Morency 2019)通过对抗训练来改进运动现实主义. 自动递减方法(蒋等. 2023; 张等. 2023a; 郭等. 2022b.) 模型运动作为离散符号序列. 和基于传播的方法(Tevet等. 2022; 黄等. 2024; 杨等. 2023)通过迭代去诺来生成运动.
最近,由于大语言模型(LLM)的快速进步(Achiam等. 2023; 赵等. 2023; Li等 2025),基于LLM的运动生成方法(Jiang等. 2023; 王等编. 2024b;Wu等2025)在产生符合复杂文字指令的高诚信运动方面取得了显著进展.

blocks.en:
However, most existing approaches are still designed for single-shot generation.
When users are dissatisfied with specific motion details, they usually have to regenerate the entire sequence from scratch.
Such a paradigm is computationally inefficient and may discard previously established kinematic context, causing unnecessary changes to motion regions that are already semantically correct.
This limitation is particularly problematic in real-world creative workflows, where users often refine their intent progressively through feedback rather than specifying all desired details in a single instruction.
blocks.zh:
然而,大多数现有方法仍然为一发一发设计.
当用户对具体的运动细节不满时,通常必须从零开始再生整个序列.
这种范式在计算上效率低下,可能会丢弃以前确定的动能上下文,导致已经完全正确的运动区域发生不必要的变化.
这种限制在现实世界的创造性工作流程中尤其成问题,用户往往通过反馈逐步完善其意图,而不是在单一的指令中具体说明所希望的所有细节。

blocks.en:
These observations motivate a more user-centric setting, namely conversational motion generation, where motions are iteratively refined through multi-turn natural language interaction.
Unlike single-shot generation, this setting requires the system to coordinate instruction understanding, motion synthesis, localized editing, quality assessment, and long-term interaction memory.
Recent advances in multi-agent systems ( Cardoso and Ferrando 2021 ; Calegari et al. 2021 ) provide a promising foundation for such role-specialized coordination.
Nevertheless, instantiating conversational motion generation with multi-agent refinement remains challenging.
First, personalized edits usually target only specific body parts or temporal segments, but naive refinement may unintentionally alter already correct motion regions and compromise global semantic consistency.
Second, without an explicit memory mechanism, agents may repeatedly explore similar editing strategies across interaction turns, leading to redundant reasoning and inefficient refinement.
blocks.zh:
这些观察激发了一个更以用户为中心的环境,即对话运动生成,通过多回合自然语言互动来迭代地完善运动.
与单发生成不同,这种设置需要系统协调指令理解,运动合成,局部编辑,质量评估,以及长期互动记忆.
近期在多代理系统方面取得的进展(Cardoso和Ferrando 2021;Calegari等2021)为这种角色专业化协调提供了有希望的基础。
然而,通过改进多剂进行即时对话的动态生成仍然具有挑战性。
首先,个性化的编辑通常只针对特定的身体部分或时间段,但天真的完善可能会无意地改变已经正确的运动区域并损害全球语义一致性.
第二,如果没有明确的内存机制,代理商可能会反复探索跨互动回合的类似编辑策略,导致冗余推理和低效的完善.

blocks.en:
To address these challenges, we propose SMART , a S elf-evolving M ulti- A gent R efinemen T framework for conversational motion generation.
SMART organizes multiple role-specialized agents into a closed-loop workflow for instruction rewriting, motion generation, video-text checking, and localized editing.
A semantic-guided masked motion editing mechanism is designed to use a Vision-Language Model (VLM) to ground natural-language feedback into a mask matrix, enabling precise refinement while preserving unaffected motion regions.
To reduce redundant exploration, SMART further incorporates a memory-based self-evolving strategy that
accumulates and updates generation knowledge from interaction history, allowing the system to optimize generation motion over multiple turns.
We further implement an interactive conversational platform to evaluate SMART under realistic multi-turn refinement scenarios.
Extensive experiments demonstrate that SMART effectively supports conversational motion refinement, preserves unaffected motion regions, and improves refinement efficiency across interaction rounds.
Our contributions are summarized as follows.
The main contributions of this work are summarized as follows: • We formulate conversational motion generation and propose SMART , a self-evolving multi-agent refinement framework that supports iterative text-to-motion refinement through multi-turn natural language interaction. • We design a semantic-guided masked motion editing mechanism that converts structured feedback into spatio-temporal editing masks, enabling localized refinement while preserving unaffected motion regions. • We develop a memory-based self-evolving strategy that accumulates successful failure–repair experiences and reuses them to reduce redundant exploration during multi-turn refinement.

blocks.en: Related Work
blocks.zh: 相关工作

blocks.en: Text-to-Motion Generation
blocks.zh: 文本对运动生成

blocks.en: Existing text-to-motion (T2M) methods can be broadly categorized into autoencoder-based, GAN-based, autoregressive, and diffusion-based approaches. Autoencoder-based methods ( Zhang et al. 2023b ; Zhong et al. 2023 ; Geng et al. 2024 ) learn compact latent representations to capture motion structures, while GAN-based methods ( Ahn et al. 2018 ; Xu et al. 2023 ; Ahuja and Morency 2019 ) employ adversarial learning to improve motion realism and diversity. Autoregressive methods generate discrete motion tokens sequentially. For example, MoMask ( Guo et al. 2024 ) adopts masked token prediction with residual refinement to improve generation efficiency, whereas MotionChain ( Jiang et al. 2024 ) and Motion-Agent ( Wu et al. 2025 ) incorporate language-based planning to support more complex motion tasks. Diffusion-based methods iteratively denoise motion sequences conditioned on textual descriptions. MotionDiffuse ( Zhang et al. 2024 ) introduces text-conditioned diffusion with temporal modeling, MDM ( Tevet et al. 2022 ) directly predicts clean motion samples with geometric losses, and ReMoDiffuse ( Zhang et al. 2023c ) enhances text-motion alignment through retrieval-augmented generation.

MotionDiffuse (Zhang等2024年)引入了以时间建模为条件的文本扩散,MDM (Tevet等2022年)直接预测了具有几何损失的清洁运动样本,ReMoDiffuse (Zhang等2023年c)通过取回-增强生成来增强文本-运动的对接.

blocks.en: LLM-based motion generation
blocks.zh: 基于 LLM 的运动生成

blocks.en:
Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in language understanding, task decomposition, tool invocation, and self-correction ( Chang et al. 2024 ; Ruan et al. 2023 ; Wu et al. 2023 ; Li et al. 2023 ; Wang et al. 2025b ; Wang et al. 2024a ) . These capabilities have motivated agent-based generative systems that coordinate specialized tools for complex generation and editing tasks ( Durante et al. 2024 ; Masterman et al. 2024 ) . For instance, GenArtist ( Wang et al. 2024c ) employs a multimodal agent to select and coordinate visual tools, demonstrating the potential of agents to unify generation and editing.
In motion generation, MotionGPT ( Jiang et al. 2023 ) represents motions as discrete tokens and unifies text and motion modeling within a language-modeling framework. MotionGPT-2 ( Wang et al. 2024b ) further extends this paradigm to motion generation, understanding, and editing.
We summarize the capabilities of representative motion generation and editing methods in Table 1 , comparing them across multi-turn dialogue, motion editing, automatic checking, cross-turn Context, and no extra training requirements.

blocks.en: Self-evolving Multi-agent Refinement Framework
blocks.zh: 自演多剂改进框架

blocks.en:
An overview of SMART is illustrated in Fig. 2 .
SMART formulates conversational motion generation as a multi-agent self-evolving refinement process.
The framework operates at two levels.
At the outer level, the user progressively refines an initially generated motion through a sequence of natural-language instructions, as shown in Fig. 2 (a).
At the inner level, each user instruction is resolved through agent-driven refinement cycles within SMART. It adopts a role-specialized directed workflow with explicit motion states and verification feedback.
Moreover, SMART introduces a memory-based self-evolving mechanism that records successful refinement experiences and reuses them in later interaction rounds.
In this way, the framework not only supports closed-loop motion refinement within each turn but also improves refinement efficiency across turns through accumulated historical experience.

在内部层面,每个用户指令都通过SMART内部由代理驱动的完善周期来解决. 它采用一种有作用的专门定向工作流程,并有明确的运动状态和核查反馈。
此外,SMART引入了基于内存的自演机制,记录了成功的完善经验,并在后一轮互动中再用.
这样,框架不仅支持在每个回合内改进闭路运动,而且通过积累的历史经验提高各回合的改进效率。

blocks.en: Experimental Setup

blocks.en: To comprehensively evaluate the performance and generalizability of our interactive motion generation framework,
blocks.zh: 为了全面评价我们互动运动生成框架的业绩和普遍性,

blocks.en:
We conduct experiments on two benchmark datasets: HumanML3D ( Guo et al. 2022a ) and KIT-ML ( Plappert et al. 2016 ) . These datasets cover diverse motion types, annotation styles, and levels of semantic complexity, enabling a comprehensive evaluation across different scenarios.
Note that, for the comparison experiments, we instantiate SMART with SALAD as the motion generator on both datasets.
For ablation studies, we use an MDM-based generator on HumanML3D unless otherwise specified.

我们对两个基准数据集进行实验:HumanML3D(Guo等2022a)和KIT-ML(Plappert等2016. 这些数据集涵盖了不同的运动类型,注释风格,以及语义复杂程度,使得能够对不同的情景进行全面评价.
请注意,在比较实验中,我们将SMART与SALAD作为两个数据集的运动发生器进行即时化.
为了进行消毒研究,我们使用基于MDM的生成器在HumanML3D上,除非另有说明.

blocks.en: Evaluation metrics
blocks.zh: 评价尺度

blocks.en:
Our evaluation consists of two parts.
First, we adopt standard text-to-motion metrics to measure the overall quality of generated motions.
Since standard T2M metrics mainly evaluate single-shot generation, we further introduce refinement-oriented metrics carefully designed for our conversational motion generation setting to assess the effectiveness of iterative motion editing. (1) Standard Text-to-Motion Metrics. We adopt standard quantitative metrics, including R-Precision,
FID, MM Dist and Diversity, following previous
works ( Guo et al. 2022a ) on the HumanML3D and KIT-ML test set.
These metrics jointly evaluate semantic alignment, distributional fidelity, and diversity of the generated motions. (2) Conversational Motion Evaluation Metrics. We further evaluate Text-Motion Similarity (TMS), Refinement Success Rate (RSR), and Local Preservation Ability (LPA). TMS measures the semantic consistency between the generated
motion and the target instruction using cosine similarity between text and motion embeddings. RSR reports the proportion of refinement cases accepted by the Checker within the allowed
refinement budget, reflecting the effectiveness of the closed-loop refinement process. LPA measures the similarity of unedited motion regions before and after refinement.

Table 2 compares SMART with representative methods on HumanML3D and KIT-ML. On HumanML3D, SMART (MDM) achieves the best Top-2 and Top-3 R-Precision of 0.723 and 0.827, respectively, while obtaining the lowest MM Dist of 2.901.

blocks.en: We evaluated the memory-based self-evolving module and spatio-temporal (ST) editing through ablation studies. As shown in Fig. 3 , full SMART achieved the highest R-Prec@1 and diversity. blocks.en: Conclusion
blocks.zh: 结论

blocks.en:
In this paper, we introduced the S elf-evolving M ulti- A gent R efinemen T Framework (SMART) for conversational text-to-motion generation. By integrating the Chatter, Generator, Editor, and Checker agents, SMART demonstrates
consistent improvements
in motion quality and semantic consistency. Our ablation studies highlight the crucial contributions of the four agents, with the full SMART configuration yielding superior performance over individual agents. Additionally, our evaluation of editing strategies showed that Spatio-Temporal Editing outperforms other methods, ensuring high-quality motions while maintaining temporal coherence.
